newsitem.title: JAPAN: Former Hamanaka boss moves jobs at Sumitomo.
newsitem.headline: Former Hamanaka boss moves jobs at Sumitomo.

text.p: The former boss of rogue trader Yasuo Hamanaka has resigned his post as general manager of the firm's non-ferrous metals department and taken up a new job within the company, Sumitomo Corp said on Monday.
Akio Imamura, 59, was Hamanaka's direct supervisor in the four years up until the onetime copper king confessed to running up losses on unauthorised trades that eventually totalled $2.6 billion.
Imamura has moved to a job involving metals and petroleum Sumitomo said, but it was not clear what his new duties would be and whether there was any change in his rank.

Last week the trading house announced that its chairman Tomiichi Akiyama had resigned his post due to the copper scandal. The move was largely a symbolic gesture of atonement as Akiyama was subsequently appointed a special adviser to the company.
At that time Sumitomo said Imamura and another Sumitomo board member, Ryo Yamakawa, had offered to resign over the copper scandal but did not say whether the offers would be accepted.
Hamanaka confessed last June to carrying out unauthorised trading over 10 years which incurred losses which amount to the biggest in market history.
He pleaded guilty last month to charges of fraud and forgery and faces up to 15 years in prison.
Imamura had been general manager of the non-ferrous metals department at Sumitomo since June 1992.
